opening.quote: Good morning, Tidewell Home, my name is Lotte, how can I help you?
opening.comment: You gave your name and the company name in your first turn, as the opening standard requires.

verification.quote: Can I have your full name and the order number or your postcode?
verification.comment: You asked for the full name and postcode before discussing the order, and the caller supplied both, so verification was done properly.

understanding.quote: So is the kettle you received not working?
understanding.comment: The caller had already said the parcel hasn't arrived, so asking whether the kettle was faulty was an unneeded question that suggested you hadn't listened; the actual issue was non-delivery.

resolution_accuracy.quote: Since it's been 6 days I'll send you a replacement kettle today, and you'll have it tomorrow.
resolution_accuracy.comment: Standard delivery is 2 to 4 working days and a lost-parcel investigation only opens after 10 working days, so promising a replacement tomorrow with no investigation was not per policy.

process_compliance.quote: Since it's been 6 days I'll send you a replacement kettle today, and you'll have it tomorrow.
process_compliance.comment: The parcel was not yet 10 working days overdue, so no replacement should be arranged, and the required lost-parcel investigation was not followed; no photo was requested either, and the required steps were skipped.

communication.quote: Ah, okay. Since it's been 6 days I'll send you a replacement kettle today, and you'll have it tomorrow.
communication.comment: The reply was polite overall, but the caller did not express frustration here, and your response to the earlier 'annoying' comment was acceptable; the tone was otherwise fine.

closing.comment: You did not confirm next steps in detail or ask whether the caller needed anything else before closing, so the call ended abruptly.
